instructional_purpose: Introduces the second branch of the conditional system: particles that set up a condition without imposing any truncating governance on the two verbs. For each particle it fixes what may follow it and how the response clause must be introduced.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Members of this set leave both the condition verb and the response verb in the mood they would otherwise carry, so no truncation exponent appears.
The particle for an expected future condition normally takes a perfect-form verb in the protasis while the clause refers to future time.
That perfect form encodes anticipated completion or high likelihood rather than past reference.
The connective is obligatory before a response clause that is nominal, imperative, negated, or opened by an aspectual or future marker, and optional before a bare affirmative verb.
The counterfactual particle marks the condition as not obtaining and licenses an emphatic prefix on an affirmative response and a negator on a negative one.
The compound particle is followed by a noun analysed as a topic whose predicate is obligatorily suppressed and understood as existential.
The two counterfactual particles share a single response-marking system because they share a counterfactual meaning.
The conditional particle and the homographic past-time temporal particle are distinct items with different clause structures.

concepts_taught: the three-slot oath frame of particle, element sworn by, and sworn content

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The element sworn by stands in the genitive because the oath particle governs it in the manner of a preposition.
The ta-prefixed oath particle combines only with the divine name.
The waw-prefixed oath particle is restricted to the divine name or one substitute.
Affirmative sworn content about the future takes an emphatic prefix and a verb-final emphasis suffix.
Affirmative sworn content about the past takes the emphatic prefix together with an aspectual particle instead of the verbal suffix.
Affirmative nominal sworn content takes either the emphatic particle of the إنّ family or the emphatic prefix.
Negative sworn content takes a negator and excludes the emphasis suffix.
A negator of the shape إنْ may substitute for ما in sworn negatives.
The emphatic prefix together with the emphasis suffix implies an oath even when no particle is present.
Only oaths on the divine name carry binding force in legal and formal settings.

instructional_purpose: Teaches the negation that denies a whole class rather than a single instance, and fixes the three surface shapes its negated noun takes according to whether that noun is bare, heads an annexation, or is annexation-like.
concepts_taught: class-wide negation contrasted with instance negation

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The particle governs its noun such that the noun is fixed rather than inflected, and the fixing surfaces as a short a-vowel without nunation.
When the negated noun heads an annexation it takes accusative case instead of the fixed ending.
When the negated noun is annexation-like it takes accusative case and retains nunation.
The predicate of the frame is nominative.
The homographic particle that leaves its noun nominative negates a single instance, and that noun is the topic of an ordinary nominal clause.
The predicate is frequently suppressed and understood as an existential.
The bare and the annexation-heading cases can be surface-identical, so the distinction between them is analytic rather than orthographic.
Universal statements, proverbs, and absolute denials signal the class-negating reading.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: These verbs raise their subject to the nominative and take a clause as predicate.
The predicate clause must be headed by an imperfect verb.
The principal nearness verb standardly takes no subordinating particle before its predicate.
The second nearness verb standardly takes the subordinating particle.
The hope verb always requires the subordinating particle.
Inceptive verbs never take the subordinating particle.
The presence of the particle correlates with subjunctive marking on the inner verb and its absence with indicative marking.
The hope verb is frozen, lacking an imperfect, and expresses present or future hope from a perfect shape.
One inceptive verb is homographic with a common transitive verb and is separated only by the category of what follows.
The durative reading of one inceptive verb is a stable semantic property rather than a contextual effect.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A fronted constituent keeps the case it would carry in the default order.
Fronting a verbal object typically requires a resumptive pronoun attached to the verb, and nominative marking on the fronted noun is excluded.
Fronting is obligatory when the predicate is a prepositional phrase and the topic is indefinite.
Interrogative words, the exclamatory frame, and the detached object pronoun occupy clause-initial position obligatorily.
Fronting produces restriction or exclusivity without any lexical marker of restriction.
Fronting yields a topic and comment reading and heightens contrast or emotional force.
The default order of a verbal clause is verb, then subject, then object.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The coordinating reading gives the second element the case of the first and asserts no order between the two.
Two other connectives encode immediate and delayed sequence respectively, unlike the coordinator.
The circumstantial reading introduces a clause that occupies an accusative position as a state description while its internal members keep their own cases.
The oath reading takes a genitive complement and is followed by sworn content.
The resumptive reading opens a syntactically independent sentence and coordinates nothing.
The accompaniment reading places its noun in the accusative as an object of accompaniment, one of the named object types.
The five readings can be separated by an ordered sequence of checks ending in coordination as the default.
The proclitic has exactly five major grammatical functions.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The i-vowel proclitic governs a following noun in the genitive and expresses ownership, benefit, or association.
Before an imperfect verb, the i-vowel proclitic correlates with subjunctive for purpose and with jussive for a third-person command.
The subjunctive after the purpose reading is caused by the proclitic itself.
The a-vowel proclitic marks emphasis and co-occurs with the verb-final emphasis suffix in sworn content.
After a negated copular verb the proclitic denies that the action was possible or expected, and the following verb is subjunctive.
The a-vowel proclitic at the head of a nominal clause adds emphasis without changing case.
The vowel on the proclitic is the primary evidence separating the emphatic readings from the rest.
The denial reading is semantically stronger than plain negation.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A clause headed by either subordinator functions as a single nominal constituent.
The light subordinator is followed by an imperfect verb carrying the subjunctive exponent.
The heavy subordinator is followed by an accusative nominal and a predicate, on the pattern of the emphatic particle family.
Every interpreted clause has an explicit verbal-noun paraphrase preserving the same governing relation.
Verbs of wanting, obligation, and ability select the light subordinator, while verbs of knowing, believing, hearing, and informing select the heavy one.
The interpreted clause can serve as the subject of a psychological-effect verb.
The light subordinator may also head a clause whose verb is perfect, with the same nominal function.
The clause occupies a case position even though it carries no case exponent of its own.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: An embedded report replaces the quotation frame with a particle-headed clause.
First and second person reference in the original is rebased onto the reference frame of the reporter.
The particle used after a saying verb is the i-vowel member of the emphatic particle pair, and the a-vowel member is an acceptable alternative.
No obligatory tense adjustment is imposed on the embedded clause.
Polar questions are embedded with the interrogative particle while content questions keep their question word and drop independent-clause word order.
Reporting verbs differ lexically in how much doubt they impart to the report.
Verbatim preservation is required where the wording itself carries authority.
